name: Execution through API
summary: Adversaries may attempt to leverage Application Program Interfaces (APIs) used for communication between control software and the hardware. Specific functionality is often coded into APIs which can be called by software to engage specific functions on a device or other software.

analytics.name: Analytic 1875
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies an unrecognized process on an ICS Linux host loading an ICS/vendor shared library that is normally restricted to approved control or engineering applications. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when execution violates an approved signer/hash/path/parent/process or tool allowlist, or originates from an unauthorized user/tool, and is tied to an OT asset or follow-on OT-relevant action. Suppress vendor-signed software, approved engineering utilities, diagnostics, patching, backup, and documented maintenance.

analytics.name: Analytic 2208
analytics.guidance: Monitor OPC UA server audit events for state-changing Write or Method service invocations and compare ClientUserId, ClientApplicationUri, SourceNode/MethodId, status, and arguments with the approved client/method baseline. For servers that support auditing, AuditWriteUpdateEventType and AuditUpdateMethodEventType provide an analyst-visible record of writes and state-changing method calls. Alert on successful or attempted control operations from unapproved clients/users or against methods/nodes outside the documented engineering workflow; do not describe this as Windows OS API telemetry.

analytics.name: Analytic 2239
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies Open Platform Communications (OPC) Unified Architecture (UA) method invocations or International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) 61850 Abstract Common Services Interface (ACSI) service requests arriving at a field device from a client identity not in the approved application allowlist, where the invoked method is a write or control operation rather than read/subscribe. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when execution violates an approved signer/hash/path/parent/process or tool allowlist, or originates from an unauthorized user/tool, and is tied to an OT asset or follow-on OT-relevant action. analytics.name: Analytic 2289
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies network traffic to Industrial Control System (ICS) Application Programming Interface (API) ports such as 4840 used in the Open Platform Communications (OPC) Unified Architecture (UA) or vendor-specific API ports from source Internet Protocol (IP) addresses not in the approved application client list, where the traffic pattern is consistent with write/control method invocations rather than subscription/read traffic. log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: Linux Audit SYSCALL/EXECVE/SOCKADDR records (configured audit rule): dlopen() of Industrial Control Systems (ICS) vendor shared library by process not in authorized ICS applications, followed by write-capable network connection to device subnet

log_sources.name: opcua:AuditEvent
log_sources.channel: OPC UA AuditUpdateMethodEventType/AuditWriteUpdateEventType: ClientUserId, ClientApplicationUri, SourceNode/MethodId, Status and arguments for a state-changing method/write

log_sources.name: WinEventLog:Sysmon
log_sources.channel: EventCode=7 where an ICS/vendor DLL is loaded by an image outside the authorized ICS application baseline

log_sources.name: NSM:Content
log_sources.channel: write/control method invocation from client identity not in approved application list

log_sources.name: zeek:ssl
log_sources.channel: Zeek ssl.log/TLS metadata: server_name (SNI), certificate chain/issuer/subject where available; compare with approved vendor domains/certificates
